choices.text: The amount of turn between two straight lines that meet at a point

choices.feedback: A straight line has no angle. An angle is the amount of turn between two lines.
A curved line is not an angle. An angle is formed where two straight lines meet.
A point has no angle. An angle is the amount of turn between two lines that meet.

hints: An angle is the amount of turn between two lines that meet at a point.
Think of the hands of a clock moving — that is an angle.
Two lines meeting at a point form an angle.
questions.explanation: An angle is the amount of turn between two straight lines that meet at a point.

questions.prompt: What do we call an angle that measures exactly 90 degrees?

choices.feedback: An acute angle is LESS than 90 degrees. A right angle is exactly 90 degrees.
An obtuse angle is MORE than 90 degrees but less than 180. A right angle is exactly 90.
A straight angle is 180 degrees. A right angle is exactly 90.

hints: A right angle is the corner of a square or rectangle.
It is exactly 90 degrees.
You can make a right angle with a piece of paper (the corner).
The corner of a book or notebook is a right angle.
questions.explanation: An angle that measures exactly 90 degrees is called a right angle.

choices.feedback: Exactly 90 degrees is a right angle, not an acute angle.

choices.text: More than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees
choices.feedback: More than 90 degrees but less than 180 is an obtuse angle, not an acute angle.
Exactly 180 degrees is a straight angle, not an acute angle.

hints: Acute angles are sharp — smaller than a right angle.
Think: 'acute' means sharp or small.
Compare: acute < right angle < obtuse < straight.
An acute angle is less than a quarter turn.
questions.explanation: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees (smaller than a right angle).

choices.text: More than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees

choices.feedback: Exactly 90 degrees is a right angle, not an obtuse angle.
Less than 90 degrees is an acute angle, not an obtuse angle.
Exactly 180 degrees is a straight angle, not an obtuse angle.

hints: Obtuse angles are wide — larger than a right angle but less than a straight line.
Think: 'obtuse' means blunt or wide.
Compare: acute < right angle < obtuse < straight.
An obtuse angle is between a quarter turn and a half turn.
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.

questions.prompt: Which of these angles is a right angle?

choices.feedback: The tip of a pencil is an acute angle (sharp), not a right angle.
A banana bend is a curved shape, not a right angle. A right angle is formed by two straight lines meeting at 90 degrees.

choices.text: The opening of a book at 30 degrees
choices.feedback: An opening book at 30 degrees is an acute angle. A right angle is exactly 90 degrees.

hints: A right angle is exactly 90 degrees.
The corner of a square or rectangle is a right angle.
You can check with the corner of a piece of paper.
The corner of a book or notebook is a right angle.
questions.explanation: A right angle is exactly 90 degrees. The corner of a square is a right angle.

questions.prompt: A pair of scissors opens to form an angle of 45 degrees. What type of angle is this?

choices.feedback: A right angle is exactly 90 degrees. 45 degrees is half of a right angle, so it is acute.
An obtuse angle is more than 90 degrees but less than 180. 45 degrees is acute.
A straight angle is 180 degrees. 45 degrees is acute.

hints: 45 degrees is exactly half of a right angle (90 degrees).
An acute angle is less than 90 degrees.
Since 45 < 90, the 45-degree angle is acute.
Think: a smaller angle is an acute angle.
questions.explanation: 45 degrees is less than 90 degrees, so it is an acute angle.

questions.prompt: Which angle is the largest: 30°, 120°, or 90°?

choices.feedback: 90° is a right angle. 120° is larger than 90° (obtuse), so 120° is the largest.
30° is an acute angle (less than 90°). 120° is larger.
30° < 90° < 120°, so 120° is the largest.

hints: Order the angles from smallest to largest.
90° is a right angle.
120° is more than a right angle but less than a straight line (180°).

questions.prompt: Which statement is true about the angles in a triangle?

choices.text: The three angles add up to 180 degrees
The three angles add up to 90 degrees
choices.feedback: The three angles in a triangle add up to 180 degrees, not 90.

choices.text: The three angles add up to 360 degrees
choices.feedback: 360 degrees is a full turn. A triangle's angles add up to 180 degrees.

choices.text: A triangle has only two angles
choices.feedback: A triangle has three angles (one at each corner). All three add up to 180 degrees.

hints: A triangle has three corners (vertices). Each corner has an angle.
All three angles in a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
This is like a straight line being split into three parts.
A straight line is 180 degrees.
questions.explanation: The three angles in a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
